subject: Service signal drop during morning run — confirmation and remedy
messages:
From: Penny Lane <penny.lane@finos-payments.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service signal drop noticed during morning run

Hi Avery,

We observed a gap in successful responses on our checkout flow this morning between ~08:43 and 09:05 PDT. Symptoms: a spike of HTTP 500s and a large tail-latency bump (p95 -> 1.6s, p99 -> >5s) — we saw our rate of successful token-generation callbacks drop by ~37% for the window.

Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream (we've attached a small sample of failing request IDs). This is affecting card captures for a subset of users on production.

Can you confirm whether this is eligible for an SLA remedy (downtime/credit)? We need a short confirmation and any immediate mitigation steps you recommend. Also requesting a postmortem and raw logs for the window for our compliance team.

Attaching: error_sample.log (snippet of failing requests).

Thanks,
Penny Lane
Ops Lead, Finos Payments
[Attachment: error_sample.log (text)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Penny Lane <penny.lane@finos-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service signal drop noticed during morning run

Hi Penny — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample. We're pulling evidence now. A few quick asks so we can scope eligibility and speed up the RCA:

- Can you confirm the customer-facing request-IDs and any trace ids you have for failed transactions (if different from the snippet)?
- Approximate traffic weight during the window (requests/min) and any unusual traffic patterns on your side?

We will:
- Pull raw ingress/egress traces and platform-side metrics for 08:30–09:15 PDT.
- Verify whether the event exceeds our SLO definitions for availability and whether the failure mode matches an SLA-eligible outage (availability, not client-side errors).
- If eligible, propose a proportional credit; if not eligible, we'll document the reasoning.

I'll loop in our infra team and follow up with a proposed timeline for a postmortem.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: request_for_samples.txt]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Service signal drop noticed during morning run — short technical summary

Avery — preliminary findings from the short evidence pull:

- Root cause: autoscaler mis-estimation during a rolling maintenance job. One serving shard saw a sequence of container preemptions which caused >40s of cold starts as KVS warming was throttled by backpressure.
- Window: 2027-09-14T08:42:13-07:00 -> 2027-09-14T09:02:27-07:00 (≈20m). We observed error-rate spike aligning with eviction events at 08:43 and final stabilization by 09:02.
- Impacted capacity: approx 2 out of 28 serving pods for the customer’s dedicated pool (roughly 7% of pool capacity) but because these were hot shards for the checkout path, the effective customer impact was amplified.
- Why this is SLA-relevant: this was an infrastructure-side availability regression (not client misuse) and exceeds our per-route availability SLO thresholds for the time window.

Attachments: eviction_events.json (eviction timestamps + node ids), kpi_traces.zip (ingress/latency traces).

Recommendation: offer a pro-rata credit for the affected window; customer-visible remediation already applied (rollback of autoscaler change + patch to backpressure limits). Prepare postmortem with timeline and preventative actions (autoscaler validation, warmup gating).

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eviction_events.json (json)]
[Attachment: kpi_traces.zip (zip)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Penny Lane <penny.lane@finos-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed proportional remedy and postmortem timeline

Hi Penny — thanks again for flagging this and for your patience while we investigated. Summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- Verified window: 08:42:13–09:02:27 PDT on 2027-09-14. We confirm this was an infrastructure-side degradation caused by autoscaler preemptions and cold-start amplification.
- Eligibility: This event meets our availability SLO criteria for a partial remedy.

Proposed remedy:
- 20% pro-rata service credit applied to Finos Payments’ September invoice for the affected workload tier. This is calculated against the proportional time-impact to the customer's provisioned capacity (detailed in the attached calculation).
- If you prefer an alternative (e.g., fixed-dollar credit or extended trial capacity), we're open to that — tell us what would best offset the immediate customer impact.

Postmortem & evidence:
- We attached the raw eviction trace bundle and a short postmortem outline. Full postmortem (detailed timeline, root cause, action items) will be delivered in 5 business days (by 2027-09-21).
- Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/finos-logs-9876 (raws), JIRA-RED-1372 (postmortem ticket).

Let me know if the credit approach above works, or if you'd like us to route an accelerated credit to billing. We can also schedule a 30-minute sync if you want to walk through the traces with Karthik.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll be prioritizing the autoscaler fixes to prevent recurrence.

Regards,
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192
[Attachment: postmortem-outline.pdf (pdf)]
